newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Lubumbashi is powerhouse of Zaire's copper wealth.
newsitem.headline: Lubumbashi is powerhouse of Zaire's copper wealth.

text.p: The southern city of Lubumbashi, invaded by rebels on Wednesday, is the powerhouse of Zaire's copper wealth and its layout is a living testimony to the Central African nation's colonial past.
-- Lubumbashi is named after small river on which city stands.

-- Capital of copper-producing Shaba Province ("Shaba" is KiSwahili for "copper"). The pre-eminence of the red metal is evident from the thick smoke swirling from the urban landscape, silhouetted by darkened factory chimneys.
-- Headquarters of state-owned mining giant Gecamines (Generale des Carrieres et des Mines).
-- Population: Estimated at about one million.

-- Zaire's Marxist independence prime minister Patrice Lumumba was assassinated there in 1961 when political crisis first hit what was then the Congo city named Leopoldville soon after Belgian colonists left.
-- Outstanding artistic and cultural metropolis with many painters and sculptors.
-- Air connections with the capital Kinshasa and with South Africa; rail links with South Africa, Zambia and Angola.
